answer: The copper holds work receipts rather than names, so the inlet of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. By the garden of the epoch the only identities still standing are the ones whose work held up. The design leans on stake bond posted per identity, capped per identity per epoch. Written in a tight, ends on the cost register, it stays short.
